newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed up but slightly off the day's highs on Thursday in moderate trade.
The market got an early boost from an announcement by the Bundesbank that it had no plans to issue 10 or 30 year paper before the start of 1997.
"This put a squeeze on the 10-year sector and we (guilder paper) got the benefit from that," one dealer said.
Some dealers said the market was well underpinned, with cash piles waiting on the sidelines, ready to jump in if debt prices dipped.
"There's lots of cash around but people don't want to buy at the highest level so they're waiting...but it's getting tricky," one dealer said. "There are more and more reasons to get in."
In addition to light positions, dealers pointed to thin supply in the fourth quarter and into 1997 as supporting the market.
But some dealers cautioned that the threat of a U.S. interest rate hike still weighed heavily on the market.
"We've seen a lot of buying today...but there are small signs there may be a sell-off," one dealer said.
He said the market was closely watching any data from the U.S. which would clarify the strength of the economic recovery.
A weaker than expected 3.1 percent fall in U.S. durable goods in August, the largest drop since April 1995, underpinned Treasuries today ahead of a keenly awaited five-year treasury note auction.
